affected_system: heat-health surveillance, prevention, and care coordination
alternatives: screen feasible locations against the largest access gaps for heat-health assessment and referral locations
co-optimize distributed and high-capacity locations for heat-health assessment and referral locations
pair care-access facility location with clinical escalation constraints with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Health records are privacy-preserving, population-defined, timely, and separated from service-request proxies.
Heat exposure, care seeking, reporting, and intervention effects remain distinct constructs.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain only existing approved locations for heat-health assessment and referral locations.

constraints.description: The heat-health surveillance and prevention site must respect declared land control, accessibility, permitting, safety, and operating feasibility.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: public-health preparedness director and emergency medical services lead
decision_question: Where should non-emergency assessment, respite, and referral sites operate during heat events?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The heat-health surveillance and prevention site must respect declared land control, accessibility, permitting, safety, and operating feasibility.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for heat-health assessment and referral locations passes documented checks for parcel control, legal authority, environmental review, access, capacity, and operator responsibility.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: care-access facility location with clinical escalation constraints
independence_key.primary_outcome: high-risk residents beyond timely heat-health support

intended_claim: A versioned site design for comparing declared alternatives affecting heat-health assessment and referral locations, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: high-risk residents beyond timely heat-health support
distributional gap in high-risk residents beyond timely heat-health support
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call a community facility a clinical site or safe respite without qualification.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for heat-health assessment and referral locations passes documented checks for parcel control, legal authority, environmental review, access, capacity, and operator responsibility.

title: Site heat-health assessment and respite access points
transportability_risks: Clinical coding, surveillance coverage, acclimatization, housing, and care access vary.
Small-area health estimates may be unstable or disclosure-sensitive.
